qs.q: A clinical genetics resident is reviewing dysmorphology terms. What defines a malformation in morphogenesis?
o: A structural distortion caused by mechanical uterine compression
A primary error of morphogenesis where development is intrinsically abnormal
A secondary destruction of a previously normal tissue structure
A single localized defect that causes multiple downstream anomalies
qs.e: A malformation is a primary error of morphogenesis where the developmental process is intrinsically abnormal from the start. In contrast, deformations are caused by extrinsic mechanical forces.

qs.q: A clinical genetics team discusses screening and diagnostic modalities for congenital anomalies. Which of the following combinations consists entirely of invasive methods of prenatal diagnosis?
o: Chorionic villous sampling with percutaneous cordocentesis
Obstetric ultrasound with chorionic villous sampling
qs.e: Chorionic villous sampling (CVS) and percutaneous umbilical blood sampling (cordocentesis) are invasive prenatal diagnostic procedures. Obstetric ultrasound and MRI are non-invasive imaging modalities.
